title: Pipelined streaming output coordination and graceful rejoin protocol
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Our current streaming output surface leaves ambiguity when clients reconnect after short network interruptions. Partial JSON fragments, mid-function-call tool invocations, and windowed KV cache state can cause duplicate tool calls or malformed structured outputs in downstream consumers. This ticket scopes a coordinated server/client protocol to make reconnect behavior deterministic while preserving low-latency pipelined delivery.

Goal: Define and implement a lightweight event envelope and rejoin semantics that: preserve function-call atomicity, allow safe partial-output resumption without re-executing side-effecting tool calls, enable cheap client-side deduplication, and minimize tail-latency impact for common cases. The protocol should be compatible with our HTTP/1.1 streaming endpoint (SSE-style) and be forward-compatible with a future HTTP/2/eventstream adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits a stable per-response output lineage token (output_id) at stream start and per-keypoint sequence numbers for emitted events.
Events include 'fragment' and 'boundary' types; clients can re-request after reconnect using last-acked sequence number and resume without re-triggering tool calls.
Function-call events are durably annotated with 'call_id' and 'call_effect' flags (none|idempotent|side-effect) allowing server-side enforcement of one-time execution or safe replay.
Client reconnect flow documented and implemented: client sends last_seen_seq + optional resume_hint; server responds with resume confirmation or compact replay of missing events.
Integration tests (unit + e2e) verifying: partial JSON reassembly, tool-call idempotency enforcement, duplicate suppression on rapid reconnects, and performance regression < 5% p50 latency.
SDK compatibility layer: JS and Python SDK accept the resume handshake transparently with no breaking API surface change.
A canary rollout runs on 5% of hosted inference traffic behind feature flag and shows no increased error ratio in 48h.
Docs and console release notes published (links included).
implementation_notes: Event envelope: JSONL lines with top-level fields: type, seq, output_id, ts, payload. Types: 'meta', 'fragment', 'boundary', 'function_call', 'resume_ack', 'resume_replay'.
Seq numbering: per-output monotonic integer starting at 1; server keeps a short-lived replay buffer (configurable, default 10k events or 2 minutes) for resume requests.

Resume handshake: client issues GET /v1/streams?output_id=&last_seq=&resume_hint=. Server validates output_id and either issues resume_ack (with first_seq to send next) or initiates resume_replay with compacted events.

Function-call semantics: when a function_call event has call_effect != 'none', server will ensure one of: a) execute once and mark call_id committed before returning resume_ack; or b) if call is idempotent, allow safe replay. We add a small durable call log for committed calls to support recovery (memory-backed with async persistence to datastore).

Partial-JSON handling: fragments are independent fragments of a top-level structured output (eg. JSON object fields). The client must reassemble by concatenating fragments until a 'boundary' event signals completion. The server ensures boundaries do not split function_call envelopes.

Backoff/backpressure: client should use exponential backoff with full jitter on connection failures and a short fast-retry tier for sub-second outages. Server provides 'retry_after_ms' hint in meta messages for coordinated throttling.

Trade-offs considered: keeping a long replay buffer increases memory/IO cost; chosen default is small buffer + clear guidance for SDKs to checkpoint frequently for high-throughput customers. We avoid full durable ledger for every response to keep costs low for hosted tier.

Compatibility: HTTP/1.1 SSE will use 'event: redwood' with data payload as the JSONL line. We add a minimal header 'X-Redwood-Stream-Version: 2' to signal new semantics. Older clients will ignore unknown fields; SDKs will support automatic parsing.
testing_plan: Unit tests for envelope encoding/decoding and seq bookkeeping (runtime repo).
Integration tests: simulate flaky connections and validate resume behavior using the stream-harness service (tests/runtime/stream-harness).
Load test: 48h run with 10k concurrent streaming connections to validate memory and replay buffer sizing; metrics captured to Grafana dashboard 'streaming/replay-health'.
Chaos run: inject synthetic network partitions in staging and verify no duplicate side-effects from function calls (use saved sandboxed tools).
SDK tests: add resume handshake coverage to js-sdk and python-sdk CI matrices to verify transparent resume behavior.
Security test: verify call_id and output_id entropy and unforgeability; run fuzzing on resume endpoints to prevent state confusion attacks.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy server behind feature flag to 5% of hosted traffic; SDKs in compatibility mode (clients can opt in). Monitor error rates, duplicate-tool-call metric, and p50/p95 latency.
Phase 2 (expanded): 25% traffic for 72h if canary stable. Enable short replay buffer extension for enterprise accounts behind runtime-1.20 feature flag.
Phase 3 (full): 100% rollout with deprecation notice for old stream version; provide a migration window for dedicated/private customers.
Fallback: server supports 'compat-mode' to accept old-style streaming without resume; ops can toggle to avoid customer impact during incidents.
Post-deploy: run a 7-day retrospective and update docs and runbook with incident scenarios and recovery steps.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Ava Patel: Initial design spike completed. Chosen seq-based resume vs byte-offset due to structured outputs and function-call boundaries.
2026-02-20 - Mateo Rios (Design): Reviewed event envelope; requested clearer guidance on client reassembly semantics for nested structured outputs.
2026-02-24 - Priya Singh (Eng Lead): Approved implementation plan. Action: Liam to prototype server-side call log for side-effecting calls. Target: POC by 2026-03-01.

2026-03-01 - Liam Chen: POC implemented (runtime PR 12345). POC notes: per-response in-memory call-log plus async persist to Dynamo-like store; observed 3% p50 latency increase under microbench; optimizing write batcher.
2026-03-03 - Nora Garcia (PM): Added canary gating and metrics to release checklist. Need SDK owners to add resume handshake by 2026-03-10 for canary opt-in.

2026-03-05 - QA: Added integration tests to stream-harness repo. Found edge case where extremely long fragments (>> 64KB) caused fragmentation metadata loss — plan to clip fragment size and emit explicit 'overflow' boundary.
Follow-ups: schedule design review with privacy/security to validate call log persistence properties before Phase 2 rollout.
